objectives.description: Re-derive corpus counts before writing code
Insert new advisory check block gated to report/plan
Flatten newlines, restrict to literal token, mention-suppression, bounded window
Emit log_warn for empty-designator and no-closing-bracket conditions; corpus sweep decision

approaches_tried.approach: awk variable named 'close' for bracket position
approaches_tried.reason: awk treats close as the builtin close() function name; using it as a scalar variable produces a syntax error on the line computing index(window, "]") -- renamed to close_pos

notes: Corpus re-derivation (via a scratch Python sweep script, informational only, not shipped) over every specs/ file carrying '[CARRIED-UNVERIFIED:' found 7 files: TODO.md, state.json (both task-management mirrors, not report/plan artifacts so untested against the shipped validator), the 360 report (13 opens, 9 mentions, 4 non-mention complete, 0 empty/unclosed after suppression), the 360 plan (3 opens, 1 mention, 2 non-mention complete), the 476 report (1 open, 0 mentions, 1 complete), and the archived 358 report/plan/summary (all complete, no mentions). The plan's own Research Integration section asserted '13 opens against 8 complete bracket matches' on the 360 report; re-derivation finds 7 complete (non-mention) matches, not 8 -- recorded here per the plan's own Scope-Hypothesis instruction to re-derive rather than inherit. After mention-suppression, every real corpus file yields zero empty-designator and zero unclosed-bracket flags, confirming both conditions can ship together in Phase 1 (no need to defer the no-closing-bracket condition to Phase 3 as a measured exclusion). Hand-ran the shipped check against all 5 report/plan corpus files: all [PASS] with 0 warnings. Built three throwaway fixtures (empty designator, unclosed bracket, mention-only) confirming the advisory fires correctly in both positive directions and stays silent on mentions; confirmed default-mode exit 0 and --strict exit 1 via the pre-existing total_issues branch, no new strictness logic added. bash -n and shellcheck both clean (shellcheck's only findings -- SC2329 on log_info and SC2016 on two unrelated pre-existing lines -- predate this change and are outside this phase's touched region).
